name: Law of Uniform Connectedness
description: Elements that are visibly connected by the same region, line, container, or filled background tend to be seen as a single unit before looser grouping cues are considered. Explicit connection usually outranks mere spacing or similarity.
design_relevance_note: Directly informs cards, pills, segmented controls, form grouping boxes, row highlights, and connectors/containers that tell users 'these belong together' at a glance.
myth_risk_note: Uniform connectedness is less well-established in mainstream cognitive-psychology literature than classical proximity/similarity, and one of the new sources found is an unreviewed graduate thesis rather than peer-reviewed research -- rated low rather than none because the peer-reviewed backing (Kimchi, Han et al.) is real, just more specialized and less cross-validated than the foundational Gestalt laws.
prevalence_note: The pattern itself is used constantly in modern interfaces, but the exact term 'uniform connectedness' is mostly found in perceptual-organization and HCI-adjacent writing rather than broad day-to-day UX vocabulary.

findings.description: Across three experiments using primed matching and visual search on hierarchical patterns, Kimchi found that connected regions of uniform visual properties operate as entry-level organizational units: many-element patterns were initially represented as global configuration and texture, while individuation of elements emerged later and required focused attention — direct empirical support for uniform connectedness as a grouping principle.
findings.source_title: Uniform connectedness and grouping in the perceptual organization of hierarchical patterns.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology Human Perception & Performance

findings.description: Reviewing a century of Gestalt and modern vision-science work, Wagemans et al. conclude that classical grouping principles such as proximity and similarity — along with newer principles such as uniform connectedness — remain core, empirically studied mechanisms of perceptual organization, with documented roles in contour integration and figure-ground organization.
findings.source_title: A century of Gestalt psychology in visual perception: I. Perceptual grouping and figure-ground organization.
